title: Finite direct image preserves ordinary scalar units
statement: Let $i:D\to T$ be a finite morphism of schemes in universe $u$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $R,A$ be commutative rings in $\operatorname{Type}(u+1)$, $\varphi:R\to A$ a ring map, $F$ an $R$-module sheaf on the small etale site of $D$, $G$ an $A$-module sheaf there [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and $\eta:F\to\operatorname{Res}_{D,\varphi}G$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Suppose, for every $A$-module sheaf $H$ on $D$, composition with $\eta$ induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(G,H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(F,\operatorname{Res}_{D,\varphi}H)$. Let $\eta_T$ be $i_*\eta$ followed by the inverse of the objectwise comparison $\operatorname{Res}_{T,\varphi}(i_*G)\cong i_*(\operatorname{Res}_{D,\varphi}G)$, using direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Then composition with $\eta_T$ induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(i_*G,H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(i_*F,\operatorname{Res}_{T,\varphi}H)$ for every $A$-module sheaf $H$ on $T$. No flatness, coefficient-finiteness, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Use Mathlib Sheaf.composeAndSheafify and Sheaf.adjunction for ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj. Form the comparison E_T(i_*F) → i_*(E_D F) by sheafifyLift of the base-change whiskering of the sheafification unit. The sheafification universal property gives its section formula. The sheaf scalar-adjunction unit formula then identifies its transpose with i_* of the scalar unit, followed by the inverse restriction comparison.

proof.text: Construct scalarStalkIso directly as the inverse of Point.presheafFiberCompIso followed by asIso of the stalk of toSheafify (equivalently the inverse of Point.presheafToSheafCompSheafFiberIso). The coprojection equations give its germ formula. Check the comparison against each stalkRestrict by applying isColimitOfPreserves to scalar extension and evaluating on a germ. The section formula of the sheafification lift makes both sides the germ of the same scalar-extended section.

proof.text: Under stalkIsoPi for the two coefficient rings, the stalk comparison is scalar extension of stalkIsoPi followed by PreservesProduct.iso and Pi.mapIso of the scalarStalkIso components. Equality follows by product projections and the preceding germ equation. Scalar extension is additive because restriction is additive and they are adjoint; it therefore preserves finite products. The geometric fibre is finite, so this composite is invertible, also for the empty fibre.

proof.text: Transport the isomorphism on ordinary geometric stalks through uliftSheafFiberIso and apply geometric-stalk conservativity. The transpose e:E_D F → G of η is an isomorphism: its precomposition maps on Hom are bijective by hη and the scalar adjunction, so isIso_of_coyoneda_map_bijective applies. Compose the comparison with i_*e. Its transpose is the displayed η_T by the already proved scalar-unit equation. Precomposition by this isomorphism followed by the scalar adjunction gives exactly the required Hom bijections.

lean.statement:
theorem finite_ordinary_scalar_unit
    (T : Scheme.{u}) {R A : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing R] [CommRing A]
    (φ : R →+* A) {D : Scheme.{u}} (i : D ⟶ T) [IsFinite i]
    (F : Sheaf D.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R))
    (G : Sheaf D.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A))
    (η : F ⟶ (Sheaf.restrictScalars D.smallEtaleTopology φ).obj G)
    (hη : ∀ H : Sheaf D.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A),
      Function.Bijective (fun f : G ⟶ H ↦
        η ≫ (Sheaf.restrictScalars D.smallEtaleTopology φ).map f)) :
    ∀ H : Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A),
      Function.Bijective (fun f : (lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i).obj G ⟶ H ↦
        ((lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} R) i).map η ≫
          (lowerStarCompRestrictScalarsIso φ i).inv.app G) ≫
            (Sheaf.restrictScalars T.smallEtaleTopology φ).map f)
